slides.title: Raise prices in 2027 — but only where customers are not price-sensitive

paragraphs.text: PALISADE DOCS  ·  2027 PRICING PLAN
Raise prices in 2027 — but only where customers are not price-sensitive
Why churn is rising, where pricing headroom exists, what each option is worth, and how to roll it out
Discussion document for Ravi Menon (CEO) and the leadership team  ·  December 2026 pricing decision
All figures come from the internal briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data). ARR in $M unless stated.

slides.title: Yes, raise prices in 2027, but target them: +10% for mid-market, up to contract caps for enterprise, and hold SMB until a renewal test proves it can bear an increase

paragraphs.text: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Yes, raise prices in 2027, but target them: +10% for mid-market, up to contract caps for enterprise, and hold SMB until a renewal test proves it can bear an increase
Rising churn is a promotion problem, not a price problem
•  About 94% of the 1.1-pt rise in SMB monthly churn comes from the 2,100 customers acquired by the 2025 50%-off promotion; they churn ~4.9%/month
•  Elsewhere churn barely moved: non-promo SMB 2.0→2.1%, enterprise flat. 18% of non-promo churners cite price, vs 19% of all SMB churners in 2025
•  Onboarding will help but cannot halve SMB churn: even full activation gets it to ~2.0%, not 1.55%
There is headroom in mid-market and enterprise, but it is unproven in SMB
•  Mid-market: a +10% list test cut conversion by only 0.5 pts (not significant); NRR is 112%; Inkwell is not seen in deals above 200 seats
•  Enterprise: NRR 118%, churn 0.2%/month, but only 40% of ARR renews in 2027 and 60% is capped at +7%
•  SMB competes with Inkwell's $9 plan (win rate 51%→38%). An increase breaks even if churn reacts at ~2× the 2023 rate
A targeted increase carries far less risk than a blanket 12%, but no pricing option delivers 15% growth on its own
•  The proposed +12% on every plan is worth $7.6M gross, not $10.3M, because only part of the ARR renews and caps apply. Net of churn it is $1.5–4.6M, and it loses money on SMB in the stress case
•  The targeted plan nets $2.2–3.6M. Raising prices for the promotion cohort loses money even at the 2023 churn response
•  With the plan, ARR reaches $96.4–97.8M before new customers. Reaching $98.9M needs $1.1–2.5M of new-logo ARR. NRR stays at ~112–114%
Roll out in three gated stages, with triggers that would change the plan
•  January: reprice mid-market and enterprise renewals. Q1–Q2: randomised SMB renewal test. July: SMB go/no-go. Throughout: an activation programme for the promotion cohort
•  Watch mid-market renewal churn (>1.0%/month triggers a cap at +5%) and the SMB test arm. Define one board churn metric and get a 2027 new-logo plan
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis. Ranges are base case to stress case; calculations on slides 9–11 and A1.

slides.title: We started from "raise mid-market and enterprise, freeze SMB"; the evidence backed most of it, rejected two internal claims, and changed our SMB answer

paragraphs.text: APPROACH: HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN
We started from "raise mid-market and enterprise, freeze SMB"; the evidence backed most of it, rejected two internal claims, and changed our SMB answer

Initial hypothesis (week 1): raise prices for mid-market and enterprise, where customers stay for integrations and the audit trail; freeze SMB, because the churn rise looks like a promotion effect that a price rise would make worse.

data: What would have to be true
1  The churn rise is concentrated in the promotion cohort, not the core base
Split SMB churn into promo and non-promo; compare H1 2025 with H1 2026
Non-promo SMB 2.0→2.1%; promo cohort implied 4.9%; ~94% of the SMB rise comes from the cohort
2  Core customers have not become more price-sensitive
Non-promo price citations 18% (vs 19% for all SMB in 2025). But SMB win rate against Inkwell fell 51%→38% (a sign of sensitivity at acquisition)
Supported for retention; open for acquisition
3  Mid-market and enterprise can absorb ~10% at renewal
2024 mid-market price test; NRR; churn; competitor reach; contract caps
Test: −0.5 pt conversion (not significant); NRR 112%/118%; no Inkwell above 200 seats. Mid-market churn did rise 0.6→0.8%
Largely supported (test covered new sign-ups only)
2023 rise kept ~half its value; non-promo base stable → a freeze is too cautious, a blanket rise too risky
Not supported: answer changed to "test, then decide"
5  The CFO's claim: 12% on all plans = $10.3M
Apply renewal timing, caps and churn response
6  The Customer Success claim: onboarding halves SMB churn in two quarters
Activation model (low activators churn at 3× the rate)
~2.8% if the cohort reaches normal activation; ~2.0% even if every customer activates; 1.55% is out of reach

paragraphs.text: Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis

slides.title: The churn rise sits almost entirely in the 2,100 promotion customers; non-promo SMB churn moved only 0.1 pt

paragraphs.text: 1 · WHY CHURN IS RISING
The churn rise sits almost entirely in the 2,100 promotion customers; non-promo SMB churn moved only 0.1 pt
Monthly logo churn by customer group, %
What drove the +1.1 pt rise in SMB churn (2.0% → 3.1%)
~94% of the SMB increase is the promotion cohort
•  The cohort is 36% of SMB customers but ~56% of SMB churners (103 of 183 a month). Its annualised churn is ~45%, against ~22% for other SMB customers.
•  Mid-market churn did rise from 0.6% to 0.8% (≈7% to 9% a year). The pack gives no cause; we treat it as a watch item for the mid-market price increase (slide 14).
•  The board dashboard's "1.4% → 2.3%" does not reconcile with these figures (see A2).
Source: Briefing pack Table 1 and §6. Promo-cohort churn is implied: (5,900 × 3.1% − 3,800 × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100 = 4.9%. The cohort was acquired Feb–Aug 2025, so it has no H1 2025 rate.

slides.title: Promotion customers leave when the discount ends and rarely set the product up; the rest of the base is no more price-sensitive than in 2025

paragraphs.text: 1 · WHY CHURN IS RISING
Promotion customers leave when the discount ends and rarely set the product up; the rest of the base is no more price-sensitive than in 2025
Churners citing "price / cheaper option" as main reason, %
Three signs this is about acquisition quality, not list price
share of new customers sending ≥5 documents in month 1: promo cohort vs other cohorts
churn rate of SMB customers sending <5 documents in month 1, vs those sending more
≤2 months
after the 50% discount ended, most promo churners had left. To them the "price" reason is a doubling of their bill, not the list price
non-promo SMB churners citing price, H1 2026 vs all SMB H1 2025: no new price sensitivity in retention

So what: the CFO is right that the churn rise is not about the list price, and the CEO is right that the promotion cohort is fragile. A list increase applied to the cohort would hit the group that already cites price 2.9× as often (52% vs 18%).

Source: Briefing pack Table 2, §6, §9. The share citing price is for churners who answered the exit survey. A blended 34% implies ~47% of respondents were promo churners, below their ~56% share of churners, so the survey slightly under-weights the cohort.

slides.title: An activation programme is worth running but cannot halve SMB churn: lifting the cohort to normal activation cuts SMB churn from 3.1% to ~2.8%, not 1.55%

paragraphs.text: 1 · WHY CHURN IS RISING
An activation programme is worth running but cannot halve SMB churn: lifting the cohort to normal activation cuts SMB churn from 3.1% to ~2.8%, not 1.55%
How much of the cohort's churn can activation explain? (monthly churn, %)
Implications

data: Churn of an activated SMB customer
Cohort churn explained by its 41% activation
Excess not explained (discount cliff, low intent)
Upper bound: every SMB customer activated
All at 1.35%, cohort keeps its cliff excess

paragraphs.text: •  Halving to 1.55% is not credible. It would put SMB below its pre-promotion level (2.0%) and below the pre-increase level in 2023 (1.8%). Even the upper bound only reaches ~2.0%.
•  2027 ARR effect is small: about $0.27M if the cohort reaches normal activation from January. We include $0.2M on the assumption the programme partly succeeds.

•  The bigger value is prevention. The cohort shows the cost of a deep, activation-blind discount: 41% activation and ~45% annual churn. Future acquisition offers should reward set-up (for example, documents sent), not just sign-up.

•  Price policy for the cohort: hold at the current full price through 2027. The cohort cites price 2.9× as often as other churners, so a 12% rise on it loses money even at the 2023 churn response (slide 9).

Source: Briefing pack §6, §9, §10. Assumes the 3× churn ratio for low activators (<5 documents in month 1) applies across the base, and that the cohort's activation gap explains part of its excess churn. The rest is treated as the effect of the discount ending.

slides.title: Mid-market and enterprise can carry an increase: low churn, NRR above 110%, a price test with no significant loss, and no low-cost rival in large deals

paragraphs.text: 2 · WHERE PRICE CAN GO
Mid-market and enterprise can carry an increase: low churn, NRR above 110%, a price test with no significant loss, and no low-cost rival in large deals

data: 2023 +8%: churn spiked 1.8→2.3% for 6 months, then settled at 1.9%
2024 +10% for new sign-ups: conversion 23.1% vs 23.6% (n.s.); revenue per lead +7.7%
None direct; increases capped at 7% on 60% of ARR
Inkwell $9 vs Palisade $15; win rate 51%→38% where Inkwell is considered
Integrations and audit trail (customer advisory board); Inkwell not seen above 200 seats

paragraphs.text: Caveats: the 2024 test covered new sign-ups, not renewals, and mid-market churn did rise 0.2 pts. Inkwell may reach smaller mid-market deals (≤200 seats). These shape the gates and triggers on slides 13–14.
Source: Briefing pack Table 1, §7, §8, §9. Revenue per lead in the mid-market test = 1.10 × 23.1 ÷ 23.6 − 1 = +7.7%. Annual churn = 1 − (1 − monthly)^12.

slides.title: In SMB, an increase pays only if churn reacts at less than ~2× its 2023 response, and Inkwell makes that uncertain: test before committing

paragraphs.text: 2 · WHERE PRICE CAN GO
In SMB, an increase pays only if churn reacts at less than ~2× its 2023 response, and Inkwell makes that uncertain: test before committing
Net 2027 ARR from +8% on non-promo SMB renewals, $M
Why the SMB call is a judgment, not a calculation

•  For an increase: the 2023 +8% kept about half its value in year one (1.08 × (1 − 3.6%) = +4.1%). Non-promo churn (2.0→2.1%) and price citations (19%→18%) barely moved from H1 2025 to H1 2026, despite Inkwell’s Oct 2025 launch.
•  Against: Inkwell Starter costs $9 vs Palisade SMB at $15. A 12% rise widens the gap from 67% to 87%. The SMB win rate where Inkwell is considered has already fallen from 51% to 38%.
•  Break-even: +8% stops paying if churn reacts at more than 2.1× the 2023 response (+12%: 2.0×). Best case is +$0.7M, which is small against a $16.6M base.
•  The promotion cohort fails even at 1×: its 2.9× higher price sensitivity turns +12% on $4.4M into -0.24M.

•  Our call: run a randomised +8% test on non-promo renewals in Q1–Q2 and keep the new-customer list price at $15. Roll out from July only if churn stays within the 2023 pattern. This gives up ~$0.3M of best-case upside to cap the downside.
Churn response as a multiple of the 2023 SMB price rise

Source: Briefing pack §7, §8, §11. Churn response per point of price = (0.5 pt × 6 months + 0.1 pt × 6 months) ÷ 8 pts = 0.45% of customers lost in 12 months per 1% of price. Non-promo SMB ARR = $21.0M − $4.4M = $16.6M.

slides.title: A 12% rise on every plan is worth $7.6M gross, not $10.3M, and $1.5–4.6M after the churn it triggers

paragraphs.text: 3 · WHAT EACH OPTION IS WORTH
A 12% rise on every plan is worth $7.6M gross, not $10.3M, and $1.5–4.6M after the churn it triggers
From the claimed to the realistic value of "+12% on every plan from January 2027", ARR $M
Net value by segment, $M
•  ~90% of the $2.8M overstatement is renewal timing; enterprise ARR that is mid-contract in 2027 alone accounts for $1.7M.
•  In the stress case SMB turns negative (−$1.0M) while mid-market still adds +$2.1M.
•  The value is in mid-market; SMB mainly adds risk.

Source: Briefing pack §4, §8. 12% × $86.0M = $10.32M. Not renewing in 2027: 60% of enterprise and 15% of mid-market ARR. Caps: 60% of renewing enterprise ARR limited to 7%. Churn response: see A1 for the base and stress parameters.

slides.title: The targeted plan nets $2.2–3.6M: a narrower range than the blanket 12% ($1.5–4.6M), and it limits SMB risk to a test group

paragraphs.text: 3 · WHAT EACH OPTION IS WORTH
The targeted plan nets $2.2–3.6M: a narrower range than the blanket 12% ($1.5–4.6M), and it limits SMB risk to a test group
Net 2027 ARR from pricing, $M

data: Test +8%, roll out in July if it passes

paragraphs.text: Why B over A and C: A beats B by ~$1M only if SMB reacts no worse than in 2023; in the stress case it loses $1M on SMB. C beats B by $0.3M in the base case but bets $16.6M of SMB ARR on an untested assumption. B pays ~$0.3M to find out first.

Source: Team model (A1). Base case: SMB churn response as in 2023, mid-market and enterprise as in the 2024 test. Stress case: SMB response 2× the 2023 level; mid-market and enterprise respond like SMB in 2023. Price uplift is measured at end-2027 ARR run-rate.

slides.title: Even with the targeted increase, reaching 15% growth needs at least $1.1–2.5M of new-customer ARR; pricing closes only ~28% of the $12.9M gap

paragraphs.text: 3 · WHAT EACH OPTION IS WORTH
Even with the targeted increase, reaching 15% growth needs at least $1.1–2.5M of new-customer ARR; pricing closes only ~28% of the $12.9M gap
2027 ARR bridge, recommended plan (option B), base case, $M (axis starts at $80M)
Base vs stress, $M
•  The NRR objective (>100%) is met under every option; SMB alone stays below 100% (~95–97%).
•  Without any price rise, new-logo ARR would need to be $4.7M.
•  Each 1 pt of NRR is worth $0.86M, so the baseline is as important as the price decision.

Source: Team model. Baseline = mid-2026 ARR × trailing-12-month NRR by segment (SMB 94%, MM 112%, Ent 118%), assumed to hold in 2027 without a price change. New-logo ARR is not in the briefing pack, so it is shown as the amount required.

slides.title: The recommendation by segment: raise where customers are locked in by value, hold where they are fragile, and test where the evidence is unclear

paragraphs.text: 4 · HOW TO EXECUTE
The recommendation by segment: raise where customers are locked in by value, hold where they are fragile, and test where the evidence is unclear

data: +10% at renewal from Jan 2027 (the tested level, not 12%)
NRR 112%; test showed no significant loss; integrations and audit trail make it sticky; no Inkwell above 200 seats
Up to the 7% cap where capped; +10% on uncapped renewals
NRR 118%; 0.2% churn; contract terms govern, so negotiate in the renewal cycle
Hold list price at $15 for new customers. Randomised +8% test on half of Q1–Q2 renewals; roll out from July if it passes
Stable churn and price citations, but Inkwell is hurting win rate; break-even at ~2× the 2023 response
Churns ~4.9%/month and cites price 2.9× as often; any increase loses money

paragraphs.text: Alongside pricing (in scope for the same December decision):
•  Stop deep, activation-blind acquisition discounts; tie future offers to set-up milestones (≥5 documents in month 1).

•  Define one board churn metric (logo vs revenue, customer- vs ARR-weighted) before the plan is reported (A2). Size a separate SMB response to Inkwell; it is out of scope here and the pack has no data on it.
Source: Team model, base to stress case. Net = end-2027 ARR uplift after price-driven churn. ARR affected = 2027 renewing ARR.

slides.title: Roll out in three stages with explicit go/no-go gates, so each step is backed by evidence from the one before

paragraphs.text: 4 · HOW TO EXECUTE
Roll out in three stages with explicit go/no-go gates, so each step is backed by evidence from the one before
Dec 2026
Mid-market & enterprise:
Approve +10% / cap policy; brief CS and account teams; renewal notices (90 days)
Reprice renewals from 1 Jan; track renewal rate weekly
Gate 1: renewal churn ≤ 1.0%/month and NRR on track → continue
Continue; prepare 2028 enterprise renewals (60% of ARR)
SMB non-promo:
Design randomised test: +8% vs control on renewals; new-customer list stays $15
Test live; read early churn and exit reasons monthly
Gate 2 (end June): extra churn ≤ 0.5 pt (2023 pattern) → go
If go: +8% on all renewals from July. If no-go: stop; keep the test arm
SMB promo cohort:
Freeze price; launch activation programme
Activation outreach; track documents sent
Measure activation lift vs 41% baseline
Review whether the cohort joins the 2028 price plan
Enablers:
Define the board churn metric
Monthly pricing dashboard by segment and cohort
Inkwell win-rate tracking (SMB and MM ≤200 seats)
Year-end review of elasticity for the 2028 plan
Source: Team proposal. The SMB test arms are ~1,900 non-promo customers each. Over six months a 0.5-pt monthly churn difference (≈240 vs ≈300 churners) is detectable at roughly 95% confidence.

slides.title: The board dashboard's "monthly churn 1.4% → 2.3%" cannot be reproduced from segment data; define the metric before the board sees the pricing plan

paragraphs.text: APPENDIX A2 · DATA QUALITY
The board dashboard's "monthly churn 1.4% → 2.3%" cannot be reproduced from segment data; define the metric before the board sees the pricing plan

data: ARR-weighted logo churn (proxy for revenue churn)

paragraphs.text: Why it matters

•  Every version rises (+44% to +64%), but the level and the size of the rise depend on the definition. Customer-weighted churn (2.6%) is dominated by SMB; ARR-weighted churn (1.2%) is dominated by mid-market and enterprise.
•  A blended figure hides the main finding of this deck: the rise is concentrated in one cohort.
Recommendation:
•  Report logo churn by segment and by acquisition cohort (promo vs non-promo), plus gross revenue churn, with written definitions.
Source: Briefing pack Table 1 and §10. Weighted averages of segment monthly logo churn rates for H1 2025 and H1 2026, using mid-2026 customer counts and ARR.
